Finds the edges of a raster with the Canny method: the thin lines where the values change most rapidly, as the breaks of slope on a slope map or the borders of the fields on an image. The edge cells get 1, all the others no-data.

**Toolbox folder:** Raster Processing<br>
**Status:** Certified<br>
**Keywords:** Edge detection, Canny, Raster<br>
**Authors:** Andrea Antonello<br>
**Class:** `org.hortonmachine.modules.CannyEdgeDetector`

**Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inMap` | raster file |  |  | The map on which to find the edges. |
| `pLowthres` | Double |  | `0.1` | The low threshold, as a fraction of the largest gradient of the map: the edges continue through the cells above it. |
| `pHighthres` | Double |  | `0.2` | The high threshold, as a fraction of the largest gradient of the map: the edges start from the cells above it. |
| `pRadiusgauss` | Double | cells | `2.0` | The standard deviation of the gaussian smoothing, in cells: larger values remove more noise and keep only the larger edges. |
| `pWidthgauss` | Integer | cells | `16` | The largest radius of the gaussian kernel, in cells: the kernel stops earlier where its weights become negligible. |

**Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `outMap` | output file |  | The map of the edges: 1 on the edges, no-data elsewhere. |

**References**

- Canny, J. (1986). A computational approach to edge detection. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 8(6), 679-698.
